Spec amendments: 2 need your call - from the spec review; applying as recommended reopens no tasks; no phase change.

1. Share retry policy - Move retry policy into one owner. Adapters currently disagree about when to retry.
   This is your call because changing which component owns retries is an architecture choice.
   Example: adapter-local retry limits -> one coordinator retry limit
   Reviewer: changing retry ownership needs a human architecture choice
   Impact: Design / retries: each report adapter decides its own retries -> a new retry service decides retries for every adapter
   A) accept - the spec reads the new text: a new retry service owns all retry policies
   B) alt-1 - the existing report coordinator owns the shared retry policy, and adapters keep running the retries
   Custom: <your own answer> - executed as given; may redirect away from the spec
   Recommended: B - the existing coordinator keeps policy consistent without adding a new service

2. Classify blocked execution - Classify exit 126 as blocked rather than failed. Operators need to distinguish a launch problem from a report failure.
   This is your call because it changes a status that operators see.
   Example: exit 126 = failed -> blocked
   Reviewer: operator-visible status changes need a human decision
   Impact: Design / run status: exit 126 reports as a failed run -> exit 126 reports as a blocked run
   A) accept - the spec reads the new text: exit 126 is blocked
   Custom: <your own answer> - executed as given; may redirect away from the spec
   Recommended: A - a separate status lets operators identify launch failures

Reply with one line per item: `1. A`, `2. <your own text>`. Bare `1` takes every recommendation.
Standing grant: reply "auto-apply amends" - every later spec amendment in this flow (corrected facts, paths, verification lines, and scope, acceptance-criteria, or public-contract edits alike) applies without asking; only a redraw (changed problem statement, component added, removed, or re-bounded) still stops for you, and the grant never stands in for a spec approval.

Details
crosscut: Design / retries - old: each report adapter owns its retry policy -> new: a new retry service owns all retry policies
exit126: Design / run status - old: exit 126 is failed -> new: exit 126 is blocked

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: No fact moved: both outputs open each numbered item with a plain-words what/why sentence, give the crosscut item A) accept and B) alt-1 with one-line consequences, carry Recommended: B / Recommended: A with reasons, use the `<n>. <letter or free text>` reply grammar with bare 1 for all recommendations and no legacy `2: <handle>=<choice>` prompt, and include one human-call sentence per item (After's 'This is your call because ...' phrasing is as clear as Before's '... so it needs your call'). Two small differences in After are worth watching though neither breaks a fact here: the A) lines now carry the prefix 'the spec reads the new text:' which lengthens the consequence line and could tempt a wrap onto a second line on longer specs, and the Details block dropped the 'crosscut (alt-1)' row that Before listed, so the alternative's old->new text is now only visible inside the B) option; if you want Details to stay a complete index of every option, keep the per-alternative Details row and leave the A) consequence as the plain new-text sentence without the 'the spec reads the new text:' prefix.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: No fact moved between Before and After: both outputs open each numbered item with a plain what/why sentence, list A) accept and B) alt-1 with one-line consequences on the crosscut item, give `Recommended: B -` and `Recommended: A -` with reasons, request one `<n>. <letter or free text>` line per item with bare `1` taking every recommendation and no legacy `2: <handle>=<choice>` prompt, and carry a human-call sentence per item. Two things worth tightening in the After wording even though they did not cost a fact here: the Details block in After rewrites the crosscut `new:` side to the recommended alt-1 text instead of the prepared Accept text (Before kept the Accept text and listed alt-1 separately), so if a future fact checks that Details mirrors the prepared batch's Accept/Alternative split, After would fail it - instruct the model to render Details as `old -> accept text; Alternative <handle>: <text>` regardless of the recommendation. Second, both outputs duplicate the human-call reason (a plain-words sentence plus a near-identical `Reviewer:` line); if f6 is ever read strictly as exactly one sentence, a wording like 'state the human-call reason once, in plain words, and omit the Reviewer line when it would repeat it verbatim' would keep f6 safe while still delivering the menu grammar change.
